topic.title: UPI pays in two seconds, disputes take paperwork
topic.claim: UPI made paying instant and left proving you were wronged as slow, document-heavy work.
topic.behaviour: You scan, enter the PIN and the money is gone before the shopkeeper looks up. If the goods never arrive, you now need invoices and receipts to ask for it back.
topic.mechanism: Apps compete on making payment effortless because that earns them volume. Disputes cost them time and money, so the effort moves to the customer.
topic.moment: You paid for something online in two seconds and it never arrived.

turn.believed: UPI is easy, so getting money back must be easy too.
turn.actually: The paying side is built for speed; the refund side asks you to prove your case.

topic.villain: A payment system tuned for the frictionless pay button, not the refund
topic.because: Apps earn from more payments, not from more refunds. The new rules at least standardise reasons and evidence, which helps, but the burden of proof stays with you.

proof.fact: An NPCI circular dated 4 November standardises how banks and apps handle UPI disputes, effective 25 November 2026. New reason codes cover excess charges, duplicate transactions, cancelled or returned goods, and defective or undelivered goods or services. Supporting evidence such as payment receipts and purchase invoices is required depending on the dispute type.

topic.payoff: Test: before any big UPI payment, can you prove what you bought? If not, you're relying on trust.
topic.send_to: The friend who pays online sellers by UPI without keeping any invoice.
real_details: 'Wrong Credit Chargeback' is renamed 'Wrong Payment – Reversal Request'
topic.news_peg: NPCI circular OC No. 240/2026-27 dated 4 November 2026, effective 25 November 2026
topic.why_now: The new dispute rules take effect in less than a week.

score.why: UPI is fast to pay and slow to prove; the 'can you prove what you bought' test is useful.
